purpose: This medication is used to treat bacterial infections such as urinary tract infections (UTIs), ear infections, bronchitis, and certain types of pneumonia. It can also be used to treat traveler's diarrhea and some skin infections. Your doctor chose this antibiotic because it works well against the specific type of bacteria causing your infection.
how_it_works: This medicine is actually two antibiotics working together as a team to fight bacteria more effectively. Sulfamethoxazole and Trimethoprim each block a different step that bacteria need to make a vitamin called folate, which bacteria must have to survive and grow. By blocking two steps at once, the medication stops the bacteria from multiplying and eventually kills them off.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, and diarrhea. Some people may get a skin rash or increased sensitivity to sunlight, so try to wear sunscreen and protective clothing while taking this medicine. Drinking plenty of water throughout the day can help reduce stomach upset and protect your kidneys.
warnings: Stop taking this medication and call your doctor right away if you develop a severe skin rash, blistering, peeling skin, or sores in your mouth — these can be signs of a serious reaction. Tell your doctor if you are allergic to sulfa drugs or any other antibiotics. This medicine is generally not recommended if you are pregnant, especially near your due date, or if you are breastfeeding. People with kidney or liver problems should use this medicine with caution and may need a different dose.
typical_dosing: For most common infections like UTIs, the usual adult dose is one double-strength tablet (DS tablet) taken twice a day — once in the morning and once in the evening — for 3 to 14 days depending on the infection. Always take it with a full glass of water and try to take it at the same times each day. Finish all of your medication even if you start feeling better, so the infection is completely gone.
